translationRepairs: Xiao Duola, whose courtesy name was Ruanlan, had served as a palace attendant to the Waqaghan of the Yaolian clan.
Xiao Duola, whose courtesy name was Ruanlan, was a member of the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace.
遙輦窪可汗宮人 marks affiliation with the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace (ordo), not service as a palace attendant to a living Waqaghan; the repair restores that institutional sense.
Xiao Duola, courtesy name Ruanlan, was a palace attendant of the Waqaghan of the Yaolian clan.
Xiao Duola, courtesy name Ruanlan, was a person of the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace.
Same Liao palace-division reading: 宮人 here is a person of 遙輦窪可汗宮, not a personal attendant of the khaghan.
He was appointed Senior Grandfather-in-law and given charge of frontier affairs along the Shanbei Road.
He was appointed Daifu Changwen and given charge of frontier affairs along the Shanbei Road.
拜大父敞穩 appoints him to the Khitan office 大父敞穩 (Daifu Changwen); rendering it as the kinship phrase “Senior Grandfather-in-law” is a mistranslation.
He was appointed Senior Grandfather-in-law and put in charge of frontier affairs on the Shanbei Road.
He was appointed Daifu Changwen and put in charge of frontier affairs on the Shanbei Road.
Same office-title correction: 大父敞穩 is Daifu Changwen, not “Senior Grandfather-in-law.”
When Yixin falsely accused and destroyed the Crown Prince, the investigation implicated Wumei, but the emperor set him free.
When Yixin, serving as northern privy commissioner, falsely accused and destroyed the Crown Prince, the investigation implicated Wumei, but the emperor set him free.
Here Yelu Yixin is the Northern Privy Commissioner, not the general with the same romanized name earlier in the chapter; the office title prevents false identification.
That autumn Yixin again reported that Wumei had privately discussed inner-palace affairs with Xiao Yangjiu, and Wumei was executed.
That autumn Yixin, serving as northern privy commissioner, again reported that Wumei had privately discussed inner-palace affairs with Xiao Yangjiu, and Wumei was executed.
The repeated office title keeps the accuser distinct from the earlier Yelu Yixin without placing Chinese characters in the English translation.
